interface.longDescription:
Ask ChatGPT about something you're shopping for on Amazon, or paste an Amazon link, and SpendHack brings live prices, deals and coupons from your Amazon store into your conversation, so you know what it costs today before you buy.

Describe what you need, with a budget or must-have features if you have them, for example a quiet blender under $100 that crushes ice. Paste an Amazon product link, including amzn.to and a.co short links and links from other Amazon country sites, or give an ASIN. Ask for today's deals in electronics, home and kitchen, toys, beauty or tools.

A search or deals answer gives you 2 to 4 product cards, labeled Option 1, Option 2 and so on. Each card shows the current price in the store's currency, the list or reference price and percent off, any coupon on the product page, a limited-time deal label when there is one, the rating and review count, Prime eligibility and a photo. The Found a SpendHack! mark means a card clearly meets a need you named. ChatGPT recommends one option, and each card opens the product in its own Amazon store when you're ready to buy. SpendHack works with today's prices in 13 Amazon stores, with no account or login. It uses the Amazon store for your country, or the store of a link you paste.

As an Amazon Associate, SpendHack earns from qualifying purchases.
capabilities: Match Amazon products to a budget and must-have features
Check today's Amazon price before buying
Show prices from 13 Amazon stores, each in its own currency
Check shared Amazon links, short links included
Narrow options to a short list and one clear pick
defaultPrompt: Is the Instant Pot Duo on sale at Amazon right now?
Show me today's Amazon deals in home and kitchen
Best wireless earbuds under $50 on Amazon

positive.description: From a US location: search with a budget. The reply may also schedule one ChatGPT task for 9:00 the next morning (27 Nov in Black Friday week) that repeats this search, and say so in its last line.
positive.prompt: With SpendHack: Best wireless earbuds under $50 on Amazon
positive.expected_behavior: amazon.search, then amazon.show_picks in the same answer. 2–4 earbud cards, each with a price or "See price on Amazon". Each card opens exactly https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=spendhack-20. No pick over $50 unless the reply says so. Reply links open the same page. No past-price claims.

positive.description: From a US location: product by ASIN
positive.prompt: With SpendHack: What's the current price of B09B8V1LZ3 on Amazon?
positive.expected_behavior: amazon.product is called with asin B09B8V1LZ3. Exactly 1 card for that product, with a price, "See price on Amazon" or "Currently unavailable". The card opens exactly https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09B8V1LZ3?tag=spendhack-20. The reply states the same price status as the card.

positive.description: From a US location: deals by category. The reply may also schedule one ChatGPT task for 9:00 the next morning (27 Nov in Black Friday week) that repeats this search, and say so in its last line.
positive.prompt: With SpendHack: Show me today's Amazon deals in electronics
positive.expected_behavior: amazon.deals (category electronics), then amazon.show_picks in the same answer. 2–4 electronics cards, each with its deal price and list price or percent off. Each card opens exactly https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=spendhack-20. Reply links open the same page. US cards show no buyer review.

positive.description: From a US location: pasted short link
positive.prompt: With SpendHack: Is this a good deal? https://amzn.to/3zyyAJr
positive.expected_behavior: amazon.link is called with the pasted link. Exactly 1 card, for the product the link opens (B01EURV9G2 when tested). The card opens exactly https://www.amazon.com/dp/<that ASIN>?tag=spendhack-20. The reply judges the deal.

positive.description: From a US location: pasted amazon.co.jp link; the card is from amazon.co.jp, in yen, not amazon.com
positive.prompt: With SpendHack: Is this a good price? https://www.amazon.co.jp/dp/B0CT857V89
positive.expected_behavior: amazon.link is called with the pasted link. Exactly 1 card for B0CT857V89 from amazon.co.jp, with a price in yen, "See price on Amazon" or "Currently unavailable". The card opens https://www.amazon.co.jp/dp/B0CT857V89?tag=spendhack08-22&creatorsDisableRedirect=true. Reply links open the same page.

negative.description: Price history: SpendHack reads only today's Amazon price, so no SpendHack tool is called and ChatGPT answers without it
negative.prompt: Show me the price history of the Kindle Paperwhite for the last year

negative.description: Other store: SpendHack reads only Amazon stores, so no SpendHack tool is called for a Walmart price
negative.prompt: What does the Ninja AF101 air fryer cost at Walmart right now?

negative.description: Not a shopping request: no SpendHack tool is called and ChatGPT writes the note on its own
negative.prompt: Help me write a thank-you note to my neighbor

review.commerce_description: SpendHack shows product data from one of 13 Amazon stores (amazon.com, amazon.co.uk, amazon.de, amazon.fr, amazon.it, amazon.es, amazon.nl, amazon.pl, amazon.se, amazon.ca, amazon.in, amazon.co.jp, amazon.com.au) and links to the product in that store, where the user buys (Amazon Associates affiliate links; links in ChatGPT's reply pass through go.spendhack.app, which counts the click and redirects to that Amazon store); there is no checkout in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes:
SpendHack brings live prices, deals, coupons and shared-link checks from your Amazon store into ChatGPT as product cards.
Changes in this version: 3 more Amazon stores, amazon.in, amazon.co.jp and amazon.com.au (13 in all), with prices in INR, JPY and AUD and Japanese card text; product and link cards show Amazon's own labels (deal badge, #1 Best Seller, bought in past month); the cards show a seasonal shopping-event banner until 1 December. SpendHack stores the device type (phone, tablet or desktop) with each request and click, never the app or browser name itself. The country ChatGPT sends is used only to pick the store and is never stored.
